planting.note: Start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost and transplant once nights stay reliably above 60F; Intenz Lipstick reblooms continuously through heat.

directions: Intenz Lipstick produces dense, upright plumes in a vivid cherry-red-to-magenta shade with violet overtones, held well above tidy green foliage. It blooms continuously from planting through hard frost and draws heavy pollinator traffic, earning it a reputation as a bee magnet in summer beds. Plants hold up well under heat and humidity with only average watering, making them dependable in containers, landscapes, or as a cut flower. Minimal deadheading is needed since the plumes stay colorful and upright for weeks at a time.

common_name: Intenz Classic Celosia (Continuous-Blooming Purple Plumed Cockscomb)

planting.note: Start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost and transplant once nights stay reliably above 60F; Intenz Classic keeps blooming right up to the first hard freeze.

directions: Intenz Classic bears slender, upright plumes in rich purple on compact, well-filled plants that work equally well as a filler in combination containers or massed in beds. Flowering is remarkably persistent, starting shortly after planting and continuing without a break until the first hard freeze stops it. The plumes attract bees steadily through the season, and plants shrug off summer heat with only average moisture. Little maintenance is needed beyond full sun and routine watering to keep the display going all summer and fall.

common_name: Intenz Dark Purple Celosia (Deer-Resistant Deep Purple Plumed Cockscomb)

planting.note: Start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost and transplant once nights stay reliably above 60F; slightly more compact than other Intenz colors.

directions: Intenz Dark Purple produces dense, upright plumes in a deep, almost black-purple shade that reads as a striking accent against silver or chartreuse companion foliage. It is slightly more compact than other Intenz colors, forming a tidy mounded habit suited to large containers as well as border plantings. Gardeners note it is seldom bothered by deer, and plants tolerate heat well with only average watering once established. Blooming runs from spring through fall with minimal deadheading required.

common_name: Century Yellow Celosia (Golden Fuzzy Plumed Cockscomb)

planting.note: Start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost and transplant once nights stay reliably above 60F; grows tall enough to serve as a thriller in container plantings.

directions: Century Yellow carries fuzzy, feathery golden-yellow plumes on tall, upright stems, giving a traditional cockscomb look with noticeably improved vigor over older plumed strains. Plants are naturally heat and drought tolerant once established and resist both deer and rabbit browsing, making them reliable in exposed beds. Flowering runs from spring through late summer and on into the first hard frost, with little care required beyond full sun and average watering. Its height suits it to the back of a border or as a central thriller in mixed containers.

common_name: Century Pink Celosia (Hot Pink Fuzzy Plumed Cockscomb)

planting.note: Start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost and transplant once nights stay reliably above 60F; shares the Century series' tall, vigorous habit.

directions: Century Pink produces fuzzy, feathery hot-pink plumes on sturdy upright stems, delivering a classic cockscomb silhouette with better garden vigor than older seed strains. It tolerates heat and drought well once rooted in and resists deer and rabbit damage, a useful trait for unfenced beds. Bloom lasts from spring through late summer and into the first hard frost with essentially no deadheading needed. Its height and strong stems make it a good thriller for large containers or a backbone plant in mixed annual borders.

planting.note: Start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost and transplant once nights stay reliably above 60F; the twisted ribbon-crest form is distinct from typical brain-shaped cockscomb.

directions: Twisted Red forms unusual, convoluted ribbon-like crests in bright red rather than the rounded brain shape typical of most cockscomb celosia, giving it strong novelty appeal in beds and cut arrangements. Plants hold an upright, well-filled habit and tolerate summer heat with only average watering once established. Flowering continues from spring through fall, and the sculptural crests work well both fresh in bouquets and air-dried for long-lasting arrangements. It needs little care beyond full sun and a well-drained site to perform reliably all season.

planting.note: Start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost and transplant once nights stay reliably above 60F; pairs with Twisted Red and Twisted Yellow to complete the series.

directions: Twisted Orange develops vivid orange, twisted ribbon-like crests on upright plants with glossy green foliage, offering a bold alternative to the familiar rounded brain-form cockscomb. The contorted crests draw attention in both landscape plantings and cut-flower displays, and they dry well for everlasting arrangements. Plants are heat tolerant and ask for only average water once established, blooming steadily from spring through fall. Full sun and routine care are all that's needed to keep the unusual blooms coming.

planting.note: Start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost and transplant once nights stay reliably above 60F; deadhead spent crests to keep fall interest going.

directions: Twisted Yellow completes the Twisted series with bright golden-yellow, contorted ribbon-like crests held above upright, well-branched plants. It performs best in rich, well-drained soil and rewards occasional deadheading of spent crests with extended fall interest. Heat tolerance is strong, and established plants need only average watering to keep blooming from spring through late summer and into the first hard frost. The unusual twisted form makes it a conversation piece in beds, containers, and cut-flower arrangements alike.

common_name: Concertina Yellow Celosia (Compact Dwarf Crested Cockscomb)

planting.note: Start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost and transplant once nights stay reliably above 60F; dwarf habit suits edging and small pots without staking.

directions: Concertina Yellow forms a dense, compact dome only about as wide as it is tall, topped with disproportionately large, bright yellow crested blooms that look oversized for such a small plant. Its dwarf, uniform habit suits edging, small containers, and mass border plantings where taller cockscomb types would overwhelm the space. Plants tolerate part sun to full sun and ask for only average watering, blooming through summer into fall with minimal fuss. It is an easy, low-maintenance choice for gardeners wanting cockscomb's novelty texture at a miniature scale.

common_name: Kelos Fire Yellow Celosia (Compact Flame-Shaped Plumed Celosia)
scientific_name: Celosia argentea var. plumosa 'Kelos Fire Yellow'

planting.note: Start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost and transplant once nights stay reliably above 60F; completes the Kelos Fire color range alongside Orange, Red, and Purple.

directions: Kelos Fire Yellow produces extra-large, flame-shaped golden-yellow plumes on compact, well-branched plants bred for season-long garden performance rather than cutting. It joins the Orange, Red, and Purple Kelos Fire colors to round out a full-spectrum landscape series known for holding its shape and color through summer heat. Plants are both heat and drought tolerant once established, flowering steadily from spring through fall with minimal deadheading. Full sun and average watering are enough to keep it compact and densely covered in color all season.
